status: SUPERSEDED by presenter-2-curtis-whitfield-driving-base.mp4 (v2, 142.083 s). v1 passed its QA gate in full but at 101.917 s it sat UNDER the documented ~120 s chunk ceiling, so a long call could still have triggered loop_mode. Never used downstream. Kept as the artifact of record; v2 reproduces its first 2378 frames byte-identically.
purpose: Reusable driving video for LatentSync. Derived from the QA-clean window of the take-2 motion base by RE-ORDERING its frames only. Built once; reused across Curtis's 32 courses and every application video he presents.

derived_from.unchanged: The take-2 motion base is untouched and verified byte-identical after this build.
derived_from.chain: approved reference presenter-2-curtis-whitfield-master.png (1672x941, sha256 c3226a91..., byte-identical throughout) -> KIE topaz/image-upscale 2x + ffmpeg conform -> presenter-2-curtis-whitfield-production-still-1920x1080.png (sha256 74e03fb4...) -> KIE kling/v2-1-pro take 2 -> this base.

why.defect: Take 2 passed 11 of 12 QA rows. The one failure was confined to the head of the clip: Curtis's lips are parted with visible teeth from about frame 5 to frame 40 (0.17-1.63 s). From frame 41 to 121 the mouth is closed, the camera is locked at 1.000x, and every gate row passes.
why.fix: Build the base out of the clean window only. No third generation was bought.

method.cost: $0.00 - ffmpeg only. No new generation, no Kling call, no TTS, no interpolation, no synthetic frames.
method.pixels: Every output frame is a copy of a decoded frame of take 2. Only the ORDER changes. No filtering, no colour work, no scaling, no upscale.
method.source_region: Frames 41-121 ONLY - the QA-clean window. Frames 1-40 carry the open mouth and are discarded; the build asserts no frame below 41 can enter the sequence. 57 distinct frames are actually used, 53-109.
method.walk: A CONTINUOUS walk along the source frame index, every step +-1, so no move contains a cut; a change of direction reads as the head settling. Wander legs are >=12 frames inside the blink-free range 60-101.
method.blinks: Take 2 contains exactly TWO blinks inside the window - 54-59 and 102-107 - located by eye on a tracked eye crop of all 81 frames. Both are emitted by walking FORWARD only, and the two ALTERNATE, so the base never repeats one identical blink. Verified structurally: every traversal is a complete in-order run and none is entered backwards or across a join.
method.joins: 22 joins, one per blink - route B2: ...101 -> [102..107] -> tail in D -> JOIN -> C; route B1: ...60 -> JOIN -> 53 -> [54..59] -> 60 -> C. Both are 7-frame skips across a blink and both are the cheapest such pairs in the window.
method.no_photometric_correction: Diane needed a per-frame multiplicative gain because Kling lifted her exposure ~9.5%. Across frames 41-121 here the total per-channel spread is 0.799/255 (~1.5%), BELOW the 1.103 RMS the source moves between two consecutive frames. Correcting it would rewrite every pixel to chase a difference smaller than the clip's own frame-to-frame noise. Left alone; every frame stays a bit-exact copy.
method.reproducible: Fixed-seed LCG (20260820). Same script + same source = same .seq.
method.encode: libx264 -preset slow -crf 12 -pix_fmt yuv420p -an -movflags +faststart (same settings as Diane's base)

blink_schedule.note: Irregular by design. Gaps run 2.0-8.08 s. The floor is 2.0 s rather than Diane's 1.4 s because a Curtis blink cycle costs more frames than hers - two of the requested short gaps could not be met and were raised to the floor.
blink_schedule.source_rate_for_comparison: Take 2 itself blinks at 35.7/min; take 1 and Diane's raw base both at 47.6/min. Diane's shipped driving base is 13.25/min.

qa_gate.run_on: The DERIVED base itself, decoded frame by frame (all 2446 frames), not on the plan.

rows.source_containment: PASS - the build asserts min/max source frame inside 41-121; actual range used 53-109, 57 distinct frames. No frame from the open-mouth head of take 2 can enter the sequence.
rows.frame_fidelity: PASS - PSNR of the encoded base against the exact re-ordered source pixels: average 53.67 dB (Y 52.69, U 57.23, V 56.32), per-frame minimum 51.11 dB across all 2446 frames. Diane's base measured 55.64 dB average. This also proves every output frame is the planned source frame.
rows.mouth_closed: PASS - the definitive check is the source set: all 57 distinct frames used were inspected by eye at 2x and every one is lips-together, no separation, no teeth. Metric control (share of the mouth box above luma 150): take 2's OPEN frames 7-40 run 0.0141-0.0243 (median 0.0203); its CLOSED frames 41-121 run 0.0062-0.0162 (median 0.0101); the derived base's maximum over all 2446 frames is 0.0119 - inside the closed distribution and below the open minimum.
rows.camera_lock: PASS - best-fit zoom against the base's own frame 1 is 1.000x at frames 612, 1223, 1834 and 2446, with ZERO residual improvement from any scale or offset. Background drift over the whole 101.9 s: wall screen 0.929, window 1.242, desk-left 1.252, desk-right 1.348 /255. Desk band 1.491.
rows.continuity_and_joins: PASS - ordinary frame-to-frame step RMS: median 1.188, p99 1.635, max 2.365. The 22 joins run 3.513-4.099 (median 3.708). Each join is therefore about three ordinary steps delivered at once - inside the range the SOURCE itself covers in 3 to 4 frames (its own 3-frame motion runs to 4.101 RMS, its 4-frame motion to 4.933). Confirmed by eye at the join on output frames 68-69: pose, expression and framing are indistinguishable across it; it does not read as a cut.
rows.blink_behaviour: PASS - 22 blinks, 12.95/min, gaps 2.0-8.08 s, irregular. Both source blinks alternate so no blink clip repeats back-to-back. Structurally verified: every traversal is a complete in-order run of 54-59 or 102-107, none entered backwards, none entered across a join. Confirmed by eye on output frames 58-74: eyes open, close at src 102, shut through src 106, reopen at src 107.
rows.identity_and_set: PASS - no cuts, transitions, scene changes, added text, logos, graphics, overlays or extra people, because no new pixels exist. Whole-frame drift vs the base's own first frame: median 2.099, max 3.384 /255.
rows.photometric_stability: PASS - maximum channel shift across the whole base 0.549/255 (1.04%), channel-mean spread 0.628/255. No correction applied or needed.
rows.loop_fit: PASS - first-vs-last whole-frame gap 1.465/255 (Diane's base 4.51). Relevant only if a call ever exceeds the base length and pingpong triggers.
rows.source_integrity: PASS - after the build: take 2 sha256 1a7740bb... unchanged, take 1 REJECTED ed424307... unchanged, production still 74e03fb4... unchanged, approved master c3226a91... unchanged.

before_first_production_use.length_check: This base is 101.917 s. Diane's is 99.625 s and was sized to exceed her longest LatentSync call (85.12 s) so loop_mode never triggers. Curtis's batches are not cut yet. Before his first render, confirm his longest single call is under 101.917 s; if any batch exceeds it, rebuild longer - the build script takes a target and costs $0.00.
before_first_production_use.unchanged_rules: Locked pipeline rules are unaffected: LatentSync stays the engine, calls stay >=40 s, padding is computed at 25 fps, LatentSync's returned audio is discarded and the 24 kHz master remuxed, delivery conformed to exactly 1920x1080.
